gaps: no parameter set fitted at 100 degC (fits span 25.0..90.0 degC); the design extrapolates

test_conditions.method: calorimetric or two-winding wattmetric loss measurement on a toroid (IEC 62044-3), >= 3 samples

requests.deliverable: loss density table Pv(f, B_pk, T, waveform) with uncertainty -> core_loss_measurement record; refitted Steinmetz / iGSE sets per temperature

gaps: no DC-bias (premagnetisation) data
requests.rationale: Steinmetz / iGSE ignore premagnetisation; volt-second imbalance or asymmetric modulation produces a DC flux whose effect on loss and permeability is unknown without data.
requests.deliverable: Pv and mu_a versus H_dc at the stated conditions -> loss reference points with dc_bias_field and dc_bias_points

gaps: initial permeability only (single small-signal value); no mu'(f), mu''(f), no temperature dependence
requests.rationale: The magnetising inductance uses the 25 degC initial permeability with an assumed residual gap; mu'(f, T) and mu''(f) are needed for the magnetising current and the small-signal model at the switching frequency.
requests.deliverable: complex permeability spectra per temperature -> amplitude_permeability / permeability_vs_temperature points

gaps: no measured winding AC resistance; Dowell / strand models only
requests.rationale: Copper loss comes from Dowell's 1-D layer model (litz as strand sub-layers); a measured R_ac(f) of the actual winding bounds the model error.

test_conditions.excitation: small-signal sinusoidal, secondary short-circuited (leakage path) and open (magnetising path)

requests.deliverable: R_ac(f) table and inductances of the prototype winding -> measurement record referencing the winding / transformer record

gaps: generic class value with a wide range; no grade-specific measurement
requests.rationale: The thermal estimate uses a class value (1-5 W/m/K range) for the ferrite; the hot-spot estimate scales with it.

project.name: AIPE Magnetics: waveform-informed DAB transformer design

limitations: Analytical models only: 1-D Dowell / 1-D leakage field, lumped or network thermal model, iGSE core loss on the volume-average flux; no finite-element, fringing, insulation-system or manufacturing analysis.

iGSE uses sinusoidal-fit Steinmetz parameters on the actual flux waveform; DC bias, minor loops and relaxation losses are not modelled; parameter sets outside their fitted temperature / flux range are flagged, not corrected.

Litz copper loss uses Dowell's layer model on strand sub-layers (bundle layers x sqrt(strands)) with the MMF profile of the arrangement; strand twisting, bundle-level eddy currents and end-turn fields are not modelled.

Temperature rise comes from a steady-state thermal network (E cores) or a lumped surface estimate (other outlines) with generic class thermal conductivities and the stated cooling assumption; no CFD, no transient, no hardware validation.
Results hold for the supplied operating point only (imported); other voltages, loads, phase shifts or modulation schemes change the currents and the flux and must be evaluated separately.
No hardware was built or measured; results are design estimates, not qualification data.
The imported waveforms are taken as given (one steady-state period, no smoothing); simulation idealisations of the source (ideal switches, no parasitics) carry over into every estimate.

checks.description: Waveform-informed analytical design relations evaluated for the selected candidate (saturation, ratio, fill, leakage, thermal limits satisfied)

limitations: Magnetics entries exported by aipe.magnetics are analytical estimates with stated assumptions; no simulation, measurement, thermal analysis or hardware qualification is claimed.

evidence.description: Converter operating point as carried by the waveform source metadata / request (switching frequency, throughput power from the mean of v_p i_p, DC voltages when recorded).
The flux linkage integral is detrended and taken with zero mean (volt-second balanced operation); iGSE ignores any DC flux component.
Magnetising inductance uses an ungapped core set with a residual mating gap of 10 um per leg.
Thermal estimate with forced convection h = 40 W/m^2/K + radiation (emissivity 0.9), ambient 40.0 degC; limits: winding hot spot <= 120 degC, core <= 110 degC.
Creepage margin 0.00 mm at every layer end and 0.20 mm between winding sections; the insulation system itself is not designed.
Peak flux density limited to 70% of Bsat at the operating temperature (0.266 T).
Primary turns raised so that the core loss density stays below 300 kW/m^3 (user ceiling).

The combined status is the weaker of the two.

limitations.statement: Analytical models only: 1-D Dowell / 1-D leakage field, lumped or network thermal model, iGSE core loss on the volume-average flux; no finite-element, fringing, insulation-system or manufacturing analysis.

iGSE uses sinusoidal-fit Steinmetz parameters on the actual flux waveform; DC bias, minor loops and relaxation losses are not modelled; parameter sets outside their fitted temperature / flux range are flagged, not corrected.

Litz copper loss uses Dowell's layer model on strand sub-layers (bundle layers x sqrt(strands)) with the MMF profile of the arrangement; strand twisting, bundle-level eddy currents and end-turn fields are not modelled.

Temperature rise comes from a steady-state thermal network (E cores) or a lumped surface estimate (other outlines) with generic class thermal conductivities and the stated cooling assumption; no CFD, no transient, no hardware validation.
Results hold for the supplied operating point only (imported); other voltages, loads, phase shifts or modulation schemes change the currents and the flux and must be evaluated separately.
No hardware was built or measured; results are design estimates, not qualification data.
The imported waveforms are taken as given (one steady-state period, no smoothing); simulation idealisations of the source (ideal switches, no parasitics) carry over into every estimate.
